goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Backup code comparison uses Array.prototype.indexOf (non-constant-time string equality) instead of a timing-safe comparison, a minor timing side-channel on code matching

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code matching is implemented as `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, which relies on normal JS equality checks rather than a timing-safe comparison. This does introduce a (likely minor) timing side-channel characteristic to the matching logic, but the diff does not show it causing incorrect behavior; it’s primarily a hardening/security-best-practice issue rather than a clearly exploitable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — Backup code comparison uses Array.prototype.indexOf (non-constant-time string equality) instead of a timing-safe comparison, a minor timing side-channel on code matching

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, backup code validation does `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. This relies on normal JS string equality via `indexOf`, which is not timing-safe and can introduce a (minor) timing side-channel when comparing a secret backup code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` is called with no type check, so a non-string `backupCode` in the request body throws an uncaught TypeError (500) instead of returning a structured ErrorCode response like the rest of the endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path checks only truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`) and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a non-string but truthy `backupCode` (e.g. `{}`, `1`, `true`), `replaceAll` will throw a `TypeError`, resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of returning a structured `{ error: ErrorCode.* }` like the rest of the handler. The diff shows no runtime type guard before calling `replaceAll`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:51 — Missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws a raw Error inside the API handler (no try/catch), producing an unhandled 500 instead of the JSON `{error}` body the client expects for every other branch

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) { ... throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError); }` without returning a JSON response. Unlike the other validation branches that `return res.status(400).json({ error: ... })`, this will bubble up as an unhandled exception and produce a generic 500 response (not the `{ error }` JSON shape the client code handles). This inconsistent error handling is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:166 — The Dialog's onOpenChange (fired by Radix's built-in ESC/overlay-click dismissal) is wired straight through to the parent with no guard at the DisplayBackupCodes step (Cancel button is hidden there per line 222, but that only removes the explicit button, not the Dialog's native dismiss paths), so a user who presses ESC or clicks outside after 2FA is already enabled server-side (backupCodes and twoFactorEnabled already persisted via prior /setup and /enable calls) can close the modal without ever seeing/copying/downloading their one-time-displayed backup codes, permanently locking themselves out of backup-code recovery with no re-display path in the API.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal the Radix <Dialog> is controlled via `open={open}` and `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` (no step-aware guard). After successful `/enable`, the code switches to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (`setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`), and the explicit Cancel button is hidden in that step (`{step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>{t("cancel")}</Button> : null}`). However, nothing prevents closing the dialog via ESC or overlay-click, which will still invoke `onOpenChange` and close the modal while on the backup-codes display step. That allows users to exit without copying/downloading/recording the backup codes that were just generated and returned by `/setup` and intended to be shown immediately after enabling.
